name: Primary Condylar Hyperplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Condylar Hyperplasia

criteria.description: Progressive unilateral enlargement of the mandibular condyle
Facial asymmetry with deviation of the chin towards the unaffected side
Radiographic evidence of condylar overgrowth on CT or panoramic radiograph
No history of trauma, infection, or neoplasm causing condylar enlargement
Development of malocclusion due to condylar overgrowth

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive unilateral condylar enlargement with mandibular asymmetry confirmed by imaging, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; histopathology is rarely required.

imaging: Panoramic radiograph showing unilateral condylar enlargement
CT scan demonstrating increased condylar volume and bone remodeling
Bone scintigraphy showing increased uptake in affected condyle
other: Histopathology (if performed) shows hyperplastic cartilage and bone without neoplastic changes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of a discrete bony mass on imaging

redFlags: Severe TMJ pain unresponsive to conservative treatment
Neurological deficits such as facial nerve palsy
references: Wolford LM, et al. Primary condylar hyperplasia: diagnosis and treatment. J Oral Maxillofac Surg. 2014.
Obwegeser HL, Makek MS. Hemimandibular hyperplasia--hemimandibular elongation. J Maxillofac Surg. 1986.
